records.source_title: Genesis Rabbah — angelic debate
records.approx_date: Genesis Rabbah generally dated to fifth century CE; later manuscript transmission and possible additions
records.parallel_summary: Angels debate whether humanity ought to be created in view of human moral conduct.
records.similarity_note: Like Q2:30, the creation decision occasions heavenly objections concerning human wrongdoing.
records.difference_note: The midrash personifies competing moral attributes and describes discord; Q2:30 specifically mentions corruption and bloodshed and announces a khalifa on earth. The Qur'anic presentation concerns divine knowledge and human responsibility.

records.source_title: Cave of Treasures (Syriac Mǝʿarath Gazzē)
records.approx_date: The Syriac Cave of Treasures is commonly treated as a late antique composition; Sergey Minov (2017) argues for a date between the middle of the sixth century and the first decades of the seventh century, a range that can overlap the Qur’anic period. This is a proposed composition date, not the date of the surviving Syriac manuscript witness or E. A. Wallis Budge’s 1927 English translation. No demonstrated direct dependence.
records.source_locator: Cave of Treasures, First Thousand Years (Adam to Yared), part 7, “The Revolt of Satan, and the Battle in Heaven,” opening paragraph; Budge 1927 translation, Syriac manuscript fol. 5b col. 2 (continuing toward fol. 6a col. 1)
records.parallel_summary: Qur’an 7:11 depicts the angels commanded to prostrate before Adam and Iblis refusing. In the Syriac Cave of Treasures, First Thousand Years part 7, Satan refuses to honor Adam, claiming that he is fire and spirit while Adam is dust, and he falls from heaven. This is a specific narrative-motif parallel; it does not establish a demonstrably earlier textual source or direct borrowing.
records.similarity_note: Both narratives explicitly connect Satan’s refusal to honor Adam with his claimed superiority over the earth-formed human; the Syriac text says Satan is fire and spirit and Adam is dust. The Qur’an gives the fire-versus-clay rationale explicitly in 7:12, immediately after 7:11.
records.difference_note: Cave of Treasures frames Satan as prince of a lower angelic order who demands worship for himself, and places the event in a Christian sacred-history account. Qur’an 7:11–12 frames a command to angels, Iblis’s refusal, and God’s interrogation. Dates and transmission histories differ; similarity is not proof of direct literary dependence.

records.parallel_summary: Gregory describes faithful young men of Ephesus who withdrew to a cave, slept for many years, and later awoke; Qur’an 18:9 introduces the Companions of the Cave and the Inscription, whose narrative continues in 18:10–26.

records.source_title: Genesis 18:1–15 — Guests and the announcement of Ishaq
records.approx_date: Composition and editing debated; most scholars place the written Pentateuch's final form in the 1st millennium BCE (commonly 6th–5th c. BCE). Oldest manuscripts: Dead Sea Scrolls, c. 3rd–1st c. BCE.
records.parallel_summary: Genesis 18:1-15: Visitors come to Abraham, who quickly serves a calf. They announce a son to his aged wife, and she laughs or reacts in astonishment at her age (11:71–72 'she laughed').
records.similarity_note: Visitors come to Abraham, who quickly serves a calf. They announce a son to his aged wife, and she laughs or reacts in astonishment at her age (11:71–72 'she laughed').
records.difference_note: In Genesis 18:8 the visitors eat. In Qur'an 11:70 and 51:27–28 they do not, and Abraham becomes afraid. Genesis has Sarah deny laughing. The Qur'an adds 'after Isaac, Jacob' (11:71) and has the wife strike her face (51:29).

records.source_title: Book of Jubilees — Scrolls of Abraham
records.approx_date: Usually dated c. 160–150 BCE; Hebrew fragments found at Qumran; full text survives in Ge'ez (Ethiopic).
records.source_locator: Jubilees ch. 12, Sefaria segments 31–32; ch. 21, segment 14
records.parallel_summary: Jubilees ch. 12, Sefaria segments 31–32; ch. 21, segment 14: Abraham is linked to sacred writings: he copies and studies 'the books of his fathers' and cites books of the forefathers. Compare 'the scriptures (ṣuḥuf) of Abraham' in 87:19.
records.similarity_note: Abraham is linked to sacred writings: he copies and studies 'the books of his fathers' and cites books of the forefathers. Compare 'the scriptures (ṣuḥuf) of Abraham' in 87:19.
records.difference_note: Jubilees has Abraham read and transmit older books (of Enoch and Noah), not receive his own scripture. Its content does not match 53:38–41.

records.source_title: Apocalypse of Abraham — Leaving father and people
records.approx_date: Usually dated late 1st–2nd c. CE (after 70 CE); survives only in Old Church Slavonic manuscripts (14th c. onward). Dating debated.
records.parallel_summary: Apocalypse of Abraham ch. VIII: God calls Abraham to separate from his father's idolatrous house. Compare 19:48: 'I will leave you and those you invoke'.
records.similarity_note: God calls Abraham to separate from his father's idolatrous house. Compare 19:48: 'I will leave you and those you invoke'.
records.difference_note: Fire from heaven destroys Terah and his house. The Qur'an has Abraham leave and pray for his father, with no destruction of the father.
